fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

`deck_sort(c: Card) -> str` was called on every card comparison during deck display sorting (84k+ calls per page load per the profiling in #5481). Each call built a sort string via string concatenation (`type_prefix + x_flag + zero-padded_cmc + card_name`), making every comparison O(string length) instead of O(1).

## What changed

- Renamed the original string-building body to `_deck_sort_str(c: Card) -> str` (private helper)
- Added module-level `DECK_SORT_KEYS: dict[str, int] = {}` 
- Extended `init()` to build `DECK_SORT_KEYS` once after `CARDS_BY_NAME` is populated: deduplicates cards by canonical name, sorts them via `_deck_sort_str`, then zip-maps to integer ranks
- Changed `deck_sort(c: Card) -> int` to a single `DECK_SORT_KEYS.get(c.name, 0)` dict lookup
- Updated `test_init_rebuilds_names_and_ignores_alias_collisions` to (a) include `type_line`/`mana_cost`/`cmc` on mock `Card` objects so `_deck_sort_str` can sort them, and (b) monkeypatch `DECK_SORT_KEYS` so `init(force=True)` with mock data doesn't pollute the module-level dict for subsequent tests

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint`: passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit magic/oracle_test.py`: 848 passed, 1 skipped — including `test_deck_sort_x_last` which verifies ordering is preserved

Fixes #6689
